- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% to avoid undershoot.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 3–5 days to align with mean reversion.
- If model forecast is significantly below recent 18-day average (e.g., 10% or more below), consider upward bias correction, especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- When sentiment is high (≥0.4) and model is forecasting a decline, reverse the direction of adjustment — model may be underestimating bullish momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates downward trends in early periods; apply a 1–3% upward bias to forecast if sentiment is negative or volatile.
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 3+ consecutive 0.1–0.2), model tends to underestimate true price; add 2–5% to forecast to account for lagged sentiment effect.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment spikes — model often overcorrects; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to sentiment before adjusting forecast.
